concept.title: The Photos buttons
concept.shortdesc: What the buttons under Photos are for on a person, an event or a source.

conbody.p: A person's page, an event and a source each have a part named . It has three round-cornered buttons in a row. Under them, the page says No attachments yet until you add a picture. When a page already has pictures, a fourth button shows, with an arrow that points down.
The same three buttons appear when you attach a copy of a source. says which file to send to family, and whether the pictures go with it.

section.title: The camera button
section.p: The first button has a camera on it. It is for a new photo, such as a photo of a certificate.

The first time, Android asks if may take pictures. Choose to allow it while you use the app, or only this time. Then the camera fills the screen, with a button to take the photo and a button to cancel. A button at the top right turns the flash on or off.

section.title: The folder button
section.p: The second button has a folder on it. It is for a picture or a scan that is already on your tablet. Android's own screen for choosing a file opens, with the pictures you saved most recently first. Choose one, or go back to leave it.

section.title: The chain button
section.p: The third button has a chain link on it. It is for a picture that is already in this tree, so you can use it again on a second person. A list of the tree's pictures opens, with a box to search them by what they show. A new tree has none yet.
